item.title: Incarico di ricerca: Phenotypic impact of FXN gene splicing reprogramming in Friedreich Ataxia cells and mice (Univ. TRENTO)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-25 12:00
Institution: Univ. TRENTO, Trento
Field: Medicine / 06/MEDS-02 Patologia generale e patologia clinica

Friedreich Ataxia (FRDA) is a rare, progressive neurodegenerative disorder caused by a GAA trinucleotide repeat expansion in the first intron of the FXN gene, resulting in reduced expression of frataxin, a mitochondrial protein essential for iron-sulfur cluster biogenesis and cellular energy metabolism. Frataxin deficiency leads to mitochondrial dysfunction and progressive neurological and cardiac manifestations, with cardiomyopathy representing a major cause of morbidity and mortality. The research program aims to investigate the molecular and functional consequences of a novel therapeutic strategy designed to increase endogenous frataxin expression through reprogramming of FXN pre-mRNA…

item.title: Incarico di ricerca: Immunological Characterization of Patients with Idiopathic Inflammatory Myopathies: Anti-CCAR1 Antibodies in Patients With and Without Malignancy and Their Association with Anti-TIF1γ Antibodies (Univ. BRESCIA)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-26 14:00
Institution: Univ. BRESCIA, Brescia
Field: Medicine / 06/MEDS-09 Malattie del sangue, oncologia e reumatologia

Idiopathic inflammatory myopathies (IIM) are rare autoimmune disorders in which malignancy represents a major cause of morbidity and mortality, particularly in cancer-associated myositis (CAM). Up to 25% of patients with IIM are diagnosed with cancer within three years before or after myositis onset. Anti-TIF1γ antibodies, detected in 7 -31% of adults with dermatomyositis, are among the strongest predictors of cancer risk. However, 25 -50% of anti-TIF1γ-positive patients do not develop cancer. Recent evidence suggests that additional autoantibodies may modulate this risk. In particular, anti-CCAR1 antibodies have been associated with reduced cancer risk and longer latency to cancer…

item.title: Incarico post-doc: Investigating the role of NEUral driven PlGF-NRP1 axis in shaping the vascular niche of recruited and self-renewing arterial MACrophages during aortic aneurysm (Finanziato dal Fondo Italiano per la Scienza FIS3 (FIS-2024-06736) CUP B53C25003640001 (ROMA "La Sapienza")

Aortic aneurysms are focal dilatations of the artery wall. Nervous and immune systems, in particular arterial macrophages, are crucial players in modulating vascular contractility. The aim of this research is to understand how nervous and immune systems interact during aortic aneurism progression and how they affect vascular function, in order to modulate immune response and counteract aortic aneurysm progression. The candidate role will be to investigate functional interactions established between neurons, immune cells and the vasculature in aorta developing aneurysm.

Interstitial lung diseases (ILDs) are heterogeneous inflammatory and fibrotic disorders whose etiology often remains unidentified. Environmental and occupational exposures may contribute to ILD onset and progression but are frequently underestimated, particularly when chronic, low-level, or multiple, because assessment relies mainly on self-reported histories. Scanning electron microscopy with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (SEM/EDS) enables objective identification and semi-quantitative characterization of inorganic particles in lung tissue and bronchoalveolar lavage.

Colorectal carcinoma (CRC) frequently harbors mutations in tumor suppressor genes—including *TP53*—that are associated with tumor progression and treatment resistance. Preliminary data suggest that ATF6 increases TRAPPC4 expression, promoting the trafficking of PD-L1 to the cell membrane. This project aims to investigate the molecular mechanisms underlying the nephroprotective effects of SGLT2 inhibition, with a focus on the role of the SIRT1/HIF-1α/HIF-2α signaling axis in diabetic nephropathy. The study will explore how empagliflozin (EMPA) modulates the balance between HIF-1α and HIF-2α through SIRT1 activation and how these pathways influence cellular adaptation to metabolic and hypoxic stress.
